analysis:
Both changed files, docs/architecture/inference.md and docs/developer/build.md, are documentation only; I found no executable code, workflow, or configuration change in the supplied units. The inference.md head excerpt (lines 5333-5433) covers Qwen27 tensor-parallel MTP, cluster stop ordering, rank ledger, and verify-row kernels. It is descriptive and matches the patch-excerpt description of changes elsewhere in the file: a cluster heartbeat file path (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE, service-health.json vs part-health.json) and a cluster-runtime-facts registration description. The build.md patch adds a note that the optimized release cache also holds the scratch directory of the native cluster worker build. It says the Metal library is deleted on restore and that the JACCL and macOS 26.2 checks run on every build, which is consistent with the existing statement that a warm cache cannot waive resource identity. This preserves the existing control and does not weaken it.

Threat-model relevance: the cache note touches the build-integrity and provider artifact contract (T-034, T-054). It states that the stale-resource safeguards stay in place, so I identified no regression. The claim that a signed release registers cluster_runtime digests automatically (inference.md patch) is a documented trust-policy statement; its implementation in the release scripts, the backend, and the provider-release.md#cluster-runtime-facts anchor is not in the supplied evidence. I did not verify it and record it as an unverified contract. I recommend the next pass confirm the claim against the actual release lane, because it affects the A-017/A-011 registration path. No unit cites an unverified attack surface. The threat model needs no update from these documentation changes. Not claimed: any audit of the underlying implementations.
